action: Take SSH off the internet and require two-factor sign-in for remote access. Patch VMware vCenter and anything still exposed to Log4Shell. Software makers: isolate signing servers and review their logs for unexpected use.
exec: Attackers were positioned for a supply-chain attack on a developer's customers; the signing step was blocked, but only just.
plain: Kaspersky found that a hacking group spent months inside a Russian software company and tried to tamper with the server that digitally signs its software. Security software blocked that attempt.

key_findings: The victim is a Russia-based developer of industrial software used mainly in Eastern Europe; Kaspersky attributes the intrusion to BO Team (Black Owl) with high confidence.
Entry was through internet-exposed SSH on a Linux terminal server with a password-authenticated service account; Log4Shell in vCenter 7.0.3 then gave root on a hypervisor.
Attackers stayed for several months and reached domain controllers, GitLab, the Ansible server, backups, SIEM and the mail server, stealing its DKIM private key.
Attempts to inject code on the code-signing server were blocked by security software; no signed malware distribution, encryption or destruction is reported.
The stolen DKIM key let them send phishing that passed sender checks, and they mostly lived off the land rather than deploying malware.
recommendations: Remove internet exposure of SSH, disable root SSH login and require two-factor sign-in for VPN, RDP and domain controllers.
Patch vCenter, hypervisors and any software still affected by Log4j.
After an intrusion reset all account passwords, reset krbtgt twice and reissue keys and certificates.
Keep backups on a non-domain server with separate credentials and test restores.
Keep logs at least 30 days and remove plaintext credentials from scripts and directory comments.

summary: Kaspersky ICS CERT describes a months-long intrusion at a Russian industrial software developer, attributed with high confidence to BO Team. The attackers entered through internet-exposed SSH, used Log4Shell in VMware vCenter to gain root on a hypervisor, and reached domain controllers, GitLab and the mail server. Their attempts to inject code on the code-signing server were blocked, and no tampered software release is reported.
title: BO Team spends months inside a Russian software developer, targets its build-signing server

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Kaspersky ICS CERT report.
